boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Barnard College
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food stops for Barnard students, featuring on-campus dining halls and local Morningside Heights staples open after hours.

cards.title: Late-Night Swipes at Diana
cards.subtitle: Barnard's Primary Late-Night Hub
cards.notes: Visit the second floor for chicken tenders, nachos, and quesadillas. It is the go-to spot for Barnard students to use meal swipes for late-night fuel during study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Barnard's on-campus cafe offering late-night hot meals like chicken tenders and nachos for students using meal swipes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Diana Center Cafe offers late-night meals from 9:00 PM to 11:45 PM, serving favorites like chicken tenders and quesadillas.
cards.source_title: Your complete guide to dining at Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Open for late-night dining until 11:45 PM most weeknights; check seasonal schedules for Saturday closures.

cards.title: The 22-Hour Campus Classic
cards.subtitle: Columbia's Late-Night Basement
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of John Jay Hall for burgers and mozzarella sticks. It is a shared Barnumbia staple known for its nearly around-the-clock availability.
cards.short_summary: A casual basement dining hall at Columbia accessible to Barnard students, famous for burgers and late-night comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: JJ's Place operates 22 hours a day, from 12:00 PM to 10:00 AM, serving as a primary late-night destination for the campus community.
cards.access_notes: Open 22 hours daily (closed 10 AM - 12 PM); accessible via student meal swipes or flex points.

cards.title: The Jumbo Slice Ritual
cards.subtitle: Oversized Slices on Broadway
cards.notes: Order a signature jumbo slice at this Broadway landmark. It is a legendary stop for students seeking a massive, affordable meal well after midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Morningside Heights institution famous for its massive pizza slices and late-night operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Koronet Pizza is known for its jumbo slices and remains open late, often until 4:00 AM on weekends.
cards.source_title: Koronet Pizza: Must-Try NY Slice in Morningside Heights
cards.access_notes: Open daily until at least midnight, with extended hours until 4:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: Seinfeld's Real-Life Diner
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Weekend Service
cards.notes: Grab a booth at this iconic diner for milkshakes or breakfast at 2 AM. It serves as a cultural touchstone and a reliable late-night study break spot.
cards.short_summary: The famous diner from Seinfeld, offering classic American fare and 24-hour service on Thursday through Sunday mornings.
cards.evidence_claim: Tom's Restaurant is open 24 hours from Thursday morning through Sunday night, providing a consistent late-night option.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours from Thursday through Sunday; closes at 1:30 AM Monday through Wednesday.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Grocery Run
cards.subtitle: Reliable Broadway Provisions
cards.notes: Stop by for prepared foods, fresh fruit, or snacks at any hour. This 24-hour market is the primary source for dorm essentials during all-nighters.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour gourmet grocery store on Broadway frequently used by students for late-night snacks and prepared meals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Westside Market location at 2840 Broadway is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7, providing continuous access to groceries and a deli counter.

cards.title: Warm Cookies Until 3 AM
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate Sweet Craving
cards.notes: Order warm chocolate chip cookies for pickup or delivery. It is a staple for celebrating finished papers or fueling late-night group projects.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in warm cookies delivered late into the night, popular for student study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies typically serves warm treats until 1:00 AM on weekdays and 3:00 AM on weekends.
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Wednesday and 3:00 AM Thursday-Saturday.

cards.title: Coffee and Strudel Til 11
cards.subtitle: The Intellectual's Late-Night Den
cards.notes: Enjoy bottomless coffee and a slice of Dobos Torte in a cozy, no-WiFi environment. It is a favorite for students writing dissertations late into the evening.
cards.short_summary: A historic, cozy cafe near campus known for its Viennese-style pastries and late evening hours for writers and students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hungarian Pastry Shop is open seven days a week until nearly 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: The Upper West Side's Hungarian Pastry Shop Is Open for Everything
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:30 PM or 11:00 PM; no WiFi available, encouraging focused work or conversation.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Smart Fridge
cards.subtitle: Automated Fresh Food
cards.notes: Find fresh salads and bowls at this automated kiosk in Barnard Hall. It is the most reliable source for healthy food on campus at 4 AM.
cards.short_summary: An automated fresh food kiosk located within Barnard Hall providing 24-hour access to healthy meals.
cards.evidence_claim: The LeFrak Byte Kiosk in Barnard Hall is available 24 hours a day for fresh salads and snacks.
cards.access_notes: Located on the 1st floor of Barnard Hall; accessible 24/7 to students with building access.

cards.title: Gourmet Sandwiches Til 11
cards.subtitle: The Late-Night Deli Upgrade
cards.notes: Order a custom deli sandwich or grab imported snacks. It is a popular alternative to standard dining hall fare for a late-night dinner or snack.
cards.short_summary: A high-end deli and market near campus offering gourmet sandwiches and specialty groceries until late evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Milano Market Westside is a popular late-night spot for students, typically open until 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Milano Market Westside | The Best NY Sandwiches
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11:00 PM; features a full-service deli counter.

cards.title: The 115th Street Grocery
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Dorm Supplies
cards.notes: Pick up groceries or hot bar items at this Broadway supermarket. It is a key resource for students living in the Quad or nearby residence halls.
cards.short_summary: A large supermarket on Broadway providing late-night access to groceries and prepared foods for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Morton Williams location at 2941 Broadway is open late, typically until 1:00 AM or 24 hours depending on seasonal student demand.
cards.access_notes: Generally open until 1:00 AM; check local signage for 24-hour service during peak academic periods.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, rooftop gardens, and historic lounges that Barnard students use to navigate their urban campus beyond the standard admissions route.

cards.title: The Green Chairs at Milstein
cards.subtitle: Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.notes: Head to the second floor of the Milstein Center to find the signature green chairs facing floor-to-ceiling windows for a sun-drenched, quiet study session.
cards.short_summary: A popular quiet study area in the Milstein Center known for its comfortable green chairs and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Milstein Center is a favorite study spot for students, specifically noted for its green chairs and large windows.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season - The Barnard Bulletin
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard and Columbia students with valid ID; library hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The Rooftop Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Milbank Hall, 5th Floor
cards.notes: Visit this state-of-the-art plant growth facility atop Milbank Hall for a peaceful escape among diverse botanical collections.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop greenhouse on Milbank Hall used for biology research and as a quiet retreat for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arthur Ross Greenhouse is a rooftop facility on Milbank Hall open to the Barnard and Columbia communities.
cards.access_notes: Located at Milbank Hall 513; check department for specific open house or visitor hours.

cards.title: The Hurston Lounge
cards.subtitle: Reid Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Relax in this historic lounge dedicated to Barnard's first Black graduate, serving as a safe and quiet meeting space in the Quad.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge in Reid Hall named in honor of alumna Zora Neale Hurston, used for meetings and quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zora Neale Hurston Lounge is located on the first floor of Reid Hall and was rededicated as a safe meeting space.
cards.source_title: Zora Neale Hurston '28: A Century of Influence | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Located within the Quad residence halls; accessible to students with Quad access.

cards.title: Diana Center Cubicles
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center
cards.notes: Utilize the desk cubicles on the third floor for a focused, quiet environment that is often less crowded than the main library.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area in the Diana Center featuring individual cubicles and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of the Diana Center is a quiet study spot with desk cubicles recommended by students for focus.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season - The Barnard Bulletin
cards.access_notes: Open during Diana Center building hours; accessible to Barnard and Columbia ID holders.

cards.entity_name: Francine A. LeFrak Foundation Center for Well-Being
cards.title: The Well-Being Center
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Explore this new hub for physical, mental, and financial wellness, featuring fitness studios and spaces for quiet reflection.
cards.short_summary: A comprehensive wellness center in Barnard Hall providing resources for physical, mental, and financial health.
cards.evidence_claim: The Francine A. LeFrak Foundation Center for Well-Being opened in 2024 in Barnard Hall as a hub for integrative wellness.
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard students, faculty, and staff; check for specific class and workshop schedules.

cards.entity_name: Jan R. and Marley Blue Lewis '05 Parlor
cards.title: Lewis Parlor
cards.subtitle: Brooks Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Study in the oldest residence hall on campus within this traditional reading room designed for quiet academic work.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room and study lounge located on the first floor of Brooks Hall in the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lewis Parlor is located on the 1st floor of Brooks Hall and serves as a reading room for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to Quad residents; non-residents may need a guest sign-in.

cards.title: The Diana Green Roof
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center, 6th Floor
cards.notes: Take a break on the ecological learning center's rooftop for fresh air and views of the campus and Upper West Side.
cards.short_summary: A sustainable green roof and ecological learning center atop the Diana Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sibyl-Levy Golden ('38) Ecological Learning Center is located on top of the Diana Center.
cards.access_notes: Access may be limited by weather or specific department events; check building signage.

cards.title: The Hewitt Tunnel Level
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, Lower Level
cards.notes: Access this all-you-can-eat dining hub through the campus tunnel system, a favorite for its diverse stations and late-night study vibes.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining hall for Barnard students, located in the lower level of Barnard Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Hewitt Dining Hall is located in the lower level of Barnard Hall and is accessible via the tunnel level.
cards.access_notes: Requires a meal swipe or payment for entry; open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

cards.title: Tower Sky Lounges
cards.subtitle: Sulzberger Tower, Floors 9-17
cards.notes: Visit the upper floors of Sulzberger Tower for shared kitchen lounges that offer some of the best skyline views on campus.
cards.short_summary: Shared kitchen and lounge spaces on the upper floors of Sulzberger Tower with expansive city views.
cards.evidence_claim: Sulzberger Tower (floors 9-17) features shared kitchen/lounge spaces on each side of the floor.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residents of Sulzberger Tower and their guests.

cards.title: Altschul Science Atrium
cards.subtitle: Altschul Hall
cards.notes: Find a table in this bright, high-ceilinged space between science labs for a productive atmosphere among STEM students.
cards.short_summary: A bright atrium in Altschul Hall used by students for studying between science classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Altschul Atrium is mentioned as an additional study area on campus for students.
cards.access_notes: Open during Altschul Hall building hours; generally accessible to the campus community.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Barnard College, from rooftop gardens to specialized libraries and student lounges.

cards.title: Arthur Ross Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Rooftop of Milbank Hall
cards.notes: Visit this tropical escape on the roof of Milbank Hall. It is open to the public for free guided tours on Wednesday afternoons from 1 PM to 3 PM.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop greenhouse featuring tropical and desert plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arthur Ross Greenhouse is open to the public free of charge on Wednesday afternoons from 1-3pm.
cards.access_notes: Public access is limited to specific Wednesday afternoon hours; student access is via the Biology department.

cards.title: Milstein Center Green Roofs
cards.subtitle: The Milstein Center
cards.notes: Relax on the tiered outdoor terraces of the Milstein Center. These green spaces offer quiet spots for study and views of the campus and city.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor terraces and green roofs designed for study and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Milstein Center features approximately 12,000 square feet of green roofs and outdoor terraces that provide inviting spaces for study and contemplation.
cards.source_title: Cheryl & Philip Milstein Center for Teaching & Learning - Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically 9 AM to 9 PM on weekdays for study spaces.

cards.title: Barnard Zine Library
cards.subtitle: Milstein Center, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Browse a unique collection of zines created by women and non-binary people. It is a great spot for creative inspiration and quiet reading.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library collection focusing on zines and feminist publications.
cards.evidence_claim: The Milstein Center houses the Library featuring a core collection of books, journals, zines, and special collections.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students and visitors during library hours; check current campus access levels.

cards.title: Futter Field
cards.subtitle: Center of Campus
cards.notes: The central lawn of Barnard's campus is the go-to spot for sunbathing, picnics, and socializing between classes during warm weather.
cards.short_summary: The primary outdoor lawn and social hub at the heart of the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Futter Field and Quad Lawn are accessible from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8 AM to 10 PM for the campus community.

cards.title: Zora Neale Hurston Lounge
cards.subtitle: Reid Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: A dedicated student lounge named after the famous alumna. It serves as a comfortable social and study space within the Quad.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge in Reid Hall honoring alumna Zora Neale Hurston.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zora Neale Hurston Lounge and the Mujeres Lounge are located on the first floor of Reid Hall.
cards.access_notes: Located within a residence hall; typically requires student ID for entry.

cards.title: Diana Center Reading Room
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center
cards.notes: Enjoy the floor-to-ceiling windows and comfortable seating in this modern reading room. It is a bright, airy space for quiet work.
cards.short_summary: A sun-drenched reading room located within the Diana Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The center also features a cafe and a reading room in addition to classrooms and exhibition galleries.
cards.source_title: Barnard College's Diana Center is a Green-Roofed Gem in NYC
cards.access_notes: Open during Diana Center building hours, generally 8 AM to 11 PM.

cards.title: Altschul Atrium
cards.subtitle: Altschul Hall
cards.notes: A spacious indoor area often used for student gatherings and informal studying. It provides a convenient meeting point near the science labs.
cards.short_summary: A large indoor atrium serving as a social and study hub in Altschul Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: There are additional study areas on campus at the Diana Center... and the Altschul Atrium for collaborative study.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours.

cards.title: Milbank Hall Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Front of Milbank Hall
cards.notes: A quiet, historic courtyard perfect for reading or birdwatching. It offers a more secluded outdoor alternative to the main campus lawns.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful outdoor courtyard located in front of the historic Milbank Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The courtyard in front of Milbank Hall and the cove just outside of the Quad... are a few of my favorite quiet, calm outdoor spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Life in NYC - Bold. Beautiful. Barnard.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community during daylight hours.

cards.title: Create at the Design Center
cards.subtitle: Milstein Center, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Use tools like 3D printers and sewing machines for your personal projects. Workshops and basic materials are often provided for free to students.
cards.short_summary: A makerspace offering tools and workshops for creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Our Design Center... give you the tools to take your ideas from concept to reality... Design, sew, mend and embroider your own clothes.
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard and Columbia students; some equipment requires a brief training session.

cards.title: Attend a Free Guest Lecture
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for free talks and panels held in this elegant room. It is a frequent venue for visiting authors and scholars.
cards.short_summary: A formal event space hosting free academic and cultural presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: Registration is not required and this event is free to attend [referring to campus events often held in Sulzberger Parlor].
cards.access_notes: Events are typically open to the student body; some may require pre-registration.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover the most productive environments across Barnard's campus, from the modern Milstein Center to historic parlors and quiet reading rooms.

cards.title: Milstein Center Second Floor
cards.subtitle: The Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.notes: Look for the signature green chairs facing floor-to-ceiling windows. This floor offers a mix of comfy chairs, desk cubicles, and collaborative tables with ample power outlets.
cards.short_summary: A popular, sun-drenched study area featuring iconic green chairs and floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Milstein Center is known for its green chairs facing big floor-to-ceiling windows and is a favorite spot for focused study.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season - The Barnard Bulletin
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard and Columbia students; volume expectations decrease as you ascend to higher floors.

cards.title: Diana Center Reading Room
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Utilize the desk cubicles along the west side for maximum focus. This room is typically quieter and less crowded than the main library spaces.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, bright reading room on the third floor of the Diana Center with desk cubicles and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The Diana Center third floor features a reading room with desk cubicles and large windows, often described as a quieter alternative to Milstein.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season - The Barnard Bulletin
cards.access_notes: Charging ports are primarily located at the desks lining the west side of the room.

cards.title: LeFrak Center Library
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Choose from 117 seats including study carrels and tables. This space serves as a reliable alternative when other libraries reach capacity.
cards.short_summary: A well-equipped study space in Barnard Hall featuring study carrels, computers, and printers.
cards.evidence_claim: The LeFrak Center in Barnard Hall contains a library space with 117 seats, including 41 study carrels and 28 table seats.
cards.source_title: Library Reviews: Barnard Library (The LeFrakBrary) - Bwog
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight most weekdays; study areas often transition to 24-hour access during reading week.

cards.title: Lewis Parlor
cards.subtitle: Brooks Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Visit this dedicated reading room for a quiet, traditional atmosphere. It is a convenient spot for residents of the Quad to decompress between classes.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room for study located on the first floor of Brooks Hall within the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jan R. and Marley Blue Lewis '05 Parlor is located on the 1st floor of Brooks Hall and is a reading room for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students; noted as a go-to spot for decompressing between classes.

cards.title: Milstein Center Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: The Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need absolute silence. Library policy dictates that volume should decrease as you ascend the building.
cards.short_summary: The designated quietest floor of the Milstein Center library for deep focus.
cards.evidence_claim: Library guidelines state that volume should decrease as you ascend the library, with the fourth floor being the quietest.
cards.access_notes: Strict quiet study expectations; open during standard library hours.

cards.title: Altschul Atrium
cards.subtitle: Altschul Hall
cards.notes: Use this space for quiet study near the science labs. It provides a convenient academic environment for students with classes in Altschul Hall.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area located within the atrium of the Altschul Hall science building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Altschul Atrium is officially listed as a location for quiet study on the Barnard campus.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically used for quiet individual work.

cards.title: Milstein Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Milstein Center, Floors 1-3
cards.notes: Reserve a room via QR code for group sessions. Rooms are available for up to 4 consecutive hours per day for Barnard and Columbia students.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms located on the first three floors of the Milstein Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can reserve Library Study Rooms on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd floors of the Milstein Center for up to 4 hours daily.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required during Fall/Spring; first-come, first-served in Summer.

cards.title: Weber Living Room
cards.subtitle: Reid Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Access this recessed space via a short staircase or lift in Reid Hall. It serves as a comfortable common area suitable for light studying.
cards.short_summary: A recessed common space in Reid Hall available for student use and residential life activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Weber Living Room is located at 118 Reid, 1st floor of Reid Hall, and is a recessed space accessible to the community.
cards.access_notes: Reservable through Residential Life & Housing; otherwise available as a student lounge.

cards.title: Sulzberger Parlor
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Study in an elegant setting featuring portraits of Barnard's founders and a fireplace. This space is often used for formal events but is a grand spot for quiet work.
cards.short_summary: An ornate, historic parlor in Barnard Hall used for both events and quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sulzberger Parlor on the 3rd floor of Barnard Hall features period furniture, portraits, and a fireplace.
cards.access_notes: Subject to closure for scheduled events; check the campus calendar for availability.

cards.title: Arthur Ross Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Milbank Hall Rooftop
cards.notes: Conduct ecological research or find inspiration among 650 plant species. This rooftop facility offers a unique, lush environment for science-focused study.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art rooftop greenhouse providing a unique botanical environment for research and study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arthur Ross Greenhouse on the roof of Milbank Hall houses approximately 650 plant species and is used for student research and ecological studies.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for biology and environmental science students; open to the community during scheduled open houses.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors of Morningside Heights that define the off-campus experience for Barnard students.

cards.title: The Main Academic Artery
cards.subtitle: Broadway between 116th and 120th Streets
cards.notes: Walk this primary corridor to transition between Barnard's gates and Columbia's main campus while passing the 116th St subway station.
cards.short_summary: The central commercial and transit spine connecting Barnard College to the rest of the Columbia University campus and Manhattan.
cards.evidence_claim: Barnard College is located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan between 116th and 120th Streets along the west side of Broadway.
cards.access_notes: Public city street accessible 24/7; contains the 116th St-Columbia University subway entrance.

cards.title: The Cultural Corridor
cards.subtitle: Amsterdam Avenue near 112th Street
cards.notes: Visit this block to find the Hungarian Pastry Shop and the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, popular for off-campus study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A major avenue east of campus known for its historic architecture, cafes, and proximity to the world's largest cathedral.
cards.evidence_claim: Amsterdam Avenue is lined with monumental sights like the Cathedral of St. John the Divine and student favorites like The Hungarian Pastry Shop.
cards.source_title: A Day in Morningside Heights | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Public avenue; businesses like Hungarian Pastry Shop have individual operating hours.

cards.title: The Southern Gateway
cards.subtitle: West 110th Street (Cathedral Parkway)
cards.notes: Head to this block for essential services like Westside Market and access to the northwest corner of Central Park.
cards.short_summary: A major cross-town street serving as the southern boundary of Morningside Heights and a hub for student groceries and park access.
cards.evidence_claim: Westside Market is located on the corner of 110th Street and Broadway, serving as an essential stop for neighborhood shopping.
cards.source_title: Your guide to navigating Morningside Heights - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Public street; Westside Market is typically open 24 hours.

cards.title: The Literary Block
cards.subtitle: West 112th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam
cards.notes: Browse the shelves at Book Culture on this block, a primary source for course texts and community literary events.
cards.short_summary: A quiet residential and commercial block home to independent bookstores and student-frequented cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: Book Culture has a location on 112th Street near Columbia that offers a wide selection of books and textbooks.
cards.source_title: Your guide to navigating Morningside Heights - Columbia Spectator
cards.access_notes: Public street; Book Culture typically opens daily at 10:00 AM.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: West 114th Street near Broadway
cards.notes: Walk past historic brownstones and Columbia residence halls on this street, which borders the iconic Butler Library.
cards.short_summary: A street dominated by university housing and Greek life brownstones, providing a classic collegiate atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: West 114th Street is a major street for campus housing, featuring six Columbia residence halls and eleven brownstones.
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require CUID for entry.

cards.title: The Pedestrian Plaza
cards.subtitle: West 116th Street (College Walk)
cards.notes: Cross Broadway to enter College Walk, a pedestrian-only stretch that serves as the heart of the Morningside campus.
cards.short_summary: A former city street transformed into a central pedestrian thoroughfare connecting the east and west sides of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: The block of 116th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam Avenue was permanently closed to vehicular traffic in 1953 and turned into College Walk.
cards.access_notes: Open to pedestrians 24/7; connects the main campus gates at Broadway.

cards.title: The Scenic Promenade
cards.subtitle: Riverside Drive at 122nd Street
cards.notes: Stroll along this drive to reach Sakura Park, famous for its cherry blossoms and views of the Hudson River.
cards.short_summary: A picturesque residential drive bordering Riverside Park, offering a quiet escape from the urban grid.
cards.evidence_claim: Sakura Park along Riverside Drive is lined with cherry blossom trees, perfect for a walk.
cards.source_title: A Day in Morningside Heights | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: Public drive and park; park is open from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM.

cards.title: The Northern Boundary
cards.subtitle: West 120th Street between Broadway and Amsterdam
cards.notes: Find Teachers College and the northern edge of the main campus on this street, which marks the transition to Manhattanville.
cards.short_summary: A key academic street housing Teachers College and providing a link to the university's northern expansion.
cards.evidence_claim: Teachers College campus is located on Broadway and occupies two blocks between West 120th St. and West 122nd St.
cards.source_title: Morningside Heights | Visit | About - Teachers College
cards.access_notes: Public street; academic buildings have specific security protocols.

cards.title: The Quiet Enclave
cards.subtitle: Claremont Avenue near 120th Street
cards.notes: Explore this residential avenue west of Broadway, home to many Barnard and Columbia faculty and graduate students.
cards.short_summary: A serene, tree-lined street known for its pre-war apartment buildings and proximity to Riverside Church.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Avenue is a residential street in Morningside Heights home to institutions like the Manhattan School of Music and university housing.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; quiet hours are generally respected.

cards.title: The Harlem Connection
cards.subtitle: West 125th Street at Broadway
cards.notes: Walk north to this historic Harlem thoroughfare to visit the Manhattanville campus and the Jerome L. Greene Science Center.
cards.short_summary: A major cultural and commercial street in Harlem that serves as the anchor for Columbia's new Manhattanville campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Manhattanville campus is located just north of 125th Street, a historic district seeing immense growth.
cards.source_title: About the Manhattanville Campus | Columbia University
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; Manhattanville campus plazas are open to the public.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the Barnard College experience, from massive sandwiches to midnight feasts.

cards.title: Big Sub
cards.subtitle: A 700-foot sandwich spanning the campus
cards.notes: Join the McIntosh Activities Council each fall to devour a massive chain of sandwiches that stretches across the campus paths.
cards.short_summary: An annual fall event where a massive, multi-hundred-foot sandwich is assembled and eaten by the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Sub is hosted by the McIntosh Activities Council (McAC) each fall since 2000, gathering the community to feast on a chain of sandwiches.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall on the Barnard campus, typically centered around Futter Field or the main walkways.

cards.title: Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Deans serving breakfast before finals
cards.notes: Head to the Diana Center the night before finals to be served tater tots and pancakes by the college president and deans.
cards.short_summary: A semi-annual tradition where faculty and staff serve breakfast to students late at night during finals week.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast happens every semester the night before finals, where faculty and staff serve students breakfast food.
cards.access_notes: Takes place in the Diana Center or LeFrak Gymnasium at midnight during finals week.

cards.title: Greek Games
cards.subtitle: Ancient-style athletic and artistic contests
cards.notes: Watch or compete in hoop rolling, chariot races, and poetry recitals in this revival of Barnard's oldest tradition.
cards.short_summary: A historic competition between classes featuring athletic and artistic events inspired by ancient Greece.
cards.evidence_claim: First held in 1903, the Greek Games involve students participating in hoop rolling, torch races, and chariot races.
cards.source_title: Bring It On! Barnard's Greek Games and Spirit Week
cards.access_notes: Held periodically in the spring on Lehman Lawn or in the gymnasium.

cards.title: Convocation
cards.subtitle: Color-coded class T-shirts at Riverside Church
cards.notes: Kick off the year at Riverside Church wearing your class-specific color for a ceremony followed by a campus block party.
cards.short_summary: The formal opening of the academic year where students wear color-coded shirts representing their graduation year.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation marks the beginning of the academic year with students dressing in color-coded T-shirts that signify their class years.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New
cards.access_notes: Ceremony held at Riverside Church followed by a block party on the Barnard campus.

cards.title: Spirit Day
cards.subtitle: A day of class pride and campus activities
cards.notes: Celebrate Barnard identity with scavenger hunts, class banners, and community activities during this annual spring event.
cards.short_summary: An annual event focused on building school spirit through class competitions and social activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Spirit Day (now part of Spirit Week) includes scavenger hunts, class banner signings, and field day activities.
cards.source_title: Bring It On! Barnard's Greek Games and Spirit Week
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April across various campus locations.

cards.title: The Green Sale
cards.subtitle: Sustainable dorm shopping during orientation
cards.notes: Shop for recycled dorm essentials like mini-fridges and decor at this massive sustainability event during move-in week.
cards.short_summary: An annual sale of donated dorm items to promote sustainability and provide affordable supplies to new students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Green Sale is held annually during NSOP, where students can purchase gently used items collected through the Give and Go Green program.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New
cards.access_notes: Occurs during New Student Orientation Program (NSOP) in late August.

cards.title: Founders Day
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the college's 1889 establishment
cards.notes: Enjoy a campus-wide barbecue and music to honor the founding of the college and the empowerment of women.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration of Barnard's founding featuring a community barbecue and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Founders Day is a celebration held in October to honor the school's founding, often featuring a barbecue for students.
cards.source_title: Political Minutes: Barnard Workers at Founder's Day
cards.access_notes: Typically held in October on the Barnard campus.

cards.title: Senior Toast
cards.subtitle: A final glass for the graduating class
cards.notes: Don cocktail attire for a formal toast to your class during your final semester, featuring custom class wine glasses.
cards.short_summary: A formal event for graduating seniors to celebrate their time at Barnard before commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Senior Toast is a tradition where seniors receive a custom class wine glass and gather for a celebratory toast.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New
cards.access_notes: Held in the spring for the graduating senior class.

cards.title: Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Illuminating College Walk for the holidays
cards.notes: Gather on College Walk for hot cocoa and a cappella performances as the winter trees are officially lit for the season.
cards.short_summary: A joint holiday celebration with Columbia University featuring the lighting of trees along College Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1998, the College has celebrated the start of the holiday season with the annual tree-lighting ceremony on Columbia's College Walk.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New
cards.access_notes: Held in early December on College Walk (116th Street).

cards.title: Take Back the Night
cards.subtitle: A march and rally against sexual violence
cards.notes: Participate in this annual April march through Morningside Heights to support survivors and advocate for safety.
cards.short_summary: An annual activist tradition involving a rally, march, and speak-out to protest sexual and domestic violence.
cards.evidence_claim: Take Back the Night has been an annual event at Barnard since 1988, featuring a rally, march, and speak-out.
cards.source_title: What Does Ending the Annual March Mean for Take Back the Night?
cards.access_notes: Held annually in April, typically starting at the Diana Center.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Barnard College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Check In for NSOP
cards.subtitle: Diana Center Lobby
cards.notes: Start your weekend by picking up your name tag and orientation schedule in the main lobby. This is the central hub for all new student resources.
cards.short_summary: The primary check-in point for the New Student Orientation Program (NSOP).
cards.evidence_claim: The Diana Center Lobby serves as the Check-In & Information Center for major campus welcome events, including orientation programs.
cards.access_notes: Open during scheduled orientation hours; typically 8:45 a.m. – 5 p.m. for check-in.

cards.title: First Group Meal
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, Lower Level
cards.notes: Head to the basement of Barnard Hall for your first meal with your orientation group. It is the traditional spot for NSOP community dining.
cards.short_summary: Barnard's main traditional dining hall, located in the lower level of Hewitt Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Hewitt Dining Hall is the first dining hall most students visit because it hosts the NSOP meals.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Barnard Hall tunnel level; requires a meal swipe or payment.

cards.title: Meet Your Orientation Group
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Lawn
cards.notes: Gather on the central lawn for icebreakers and tabling events. It is the primary outdoor space for student life activities.
cards.short_summary: A central campus green space used for student resource fairs and outdoor gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Futter Field is used for student service resource fairs and major outdoor community events like Big Sub.
cards.access_notes: Open campus lawn; specific events may have set times.

cards.title: Find a Study Nook
cards.subtitle: 2nd Floor, Chen Library
cards.notes: Scope out the famous swiveling green chairs facing the floor-to-ceiling windows. It is the go-to spot for a quiet moment between sessions.
cards.short_summary: The Cheryl and Philip Milstein Center for Teaching and Learning, featuring iconic green study chairs.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Milstein Center is known for its green chairs that face large floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season - The Barnard Bulletin
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary; typically open late during the academic semester.

cards.title: Grab a Smoothie
cards.subtitle: Diana Center, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Visit the second floor for a custom smoothie or a slice of the student-favorite white pizza. It is a bright, social alternative to the main hall.
cards.short_summary: A food court style dining location offering smoothies, pizza, and customizable bowls.
cards.evidence_claim: The Diana Center Café is located on the second floor and is well-known for its smoothie station and pizza.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday; typically closed on Saturdays.

cards.title: Visit the Rooftop Plants
cards.subtitle: Milbank Hall Roof
cards.notes: Take a break in this glass-walled sanctuary atop Milbank Hall. It houses a diverse botanical collection and offers a quiet escape.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art plant growth facility and teaching collection on the roof of Milbank Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arthur Ross Greenhouse is a biodiversity learning site built on the roof of Milbank Hall.
cards.access_notes: Building hours for Milbank are typically 8 a.m. – 11 p.m. weekdays.

cards.title: Observe a Dance Class
cards.subtitle: Barnard Hall, Various Floors
cards.notes: Stop by the studios to watch a ballet or modern dance session. The department often opens classes for observation during welcome weekends.
cards.short_summary: The home of Barnard's Dance Department, featuring multiple professional studios.
cards.evidence_claim: During Family Weekend and orientation events, students and families can observe various dance classes in Barnard Hall.
cards.access_notes: Studios are located on the lower level, 1st, and 3rd floors.

cards.title: See the Campus Icon
cards.subtitle: Near Diana Center Terrace
cards.notes: Visit the site of Barnard's most beloved tree. Though the original 'Maggie' was replaced, the new tree remains a symbol of campus spirit.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic campus landmark and gathering spot for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The magnolia tree is a cherished campus tradition, with a replacement planted near the Diana Center terrace.
cards.source_title: Maggie's Gone, But Not Forgotten - Bwog
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Evening Coffee Run
cards.subtitle: Diana Center, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Grab a late-afternoon latte or snack at this popular cafe. It is a central meeting spot for students living in the Quad.
cards.short_summary: A campus cafe serving coffee, tea, and grab-and-go food items.
cards.evidence_claim: Liz's Place is located on the 1st floor of the Diana Center and offers coffee, pastries, and snacks.
cards.access_notes: Open until 5:30 p.m. on Fridays and 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

cards.title: Learn the Traditions
cards.subtitle: Event Spaces
cards.notes: End your weekend by learning about Midnight Breakfast, where deans serve tater tots to students. It is Barnard's biggest semesterly event.
cards.short_summary: A major Barnard tradition where faculty and staff serve breakfast to students before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is Barnard's biggest tradition, held in the Diana Center the night before finals start.
cards.source_title: Barnard's Bold Campus Traditions: Old and New | Barnard College
cards.access_notes: The tradition occurs once per semester; first-years are let in first in the Fall.
